estandares: Expreso posturas argumentadas sobre asuntos sociales y ambientales. Manifiesto deseos, arrepentimientos y obligaciones con estructuras precisas.
competencias: Aplicar patrones de gerundio e infinitivo; usar modales de obligación, consejo, posibilidad y necesidad; expresar deseos con I wish / If only; discutir derechos humanos y ambiente.
componentes: Pensamiento crítico, comunicación, colaboración y creatividad.

proyecto.descripcion_es: Cada estudiante elige una causa social o ambiental y prepara un discurso de tres minutos: qué se debería hacer (modales), qué desearía que fuera distinto (I wish) y qué acciones propone.
proyecto.descripcion_en: Each student chooses a social or environmental cause and prepares a three-minute speech: what should be done (modals), what they wish were different (I wish) and what actions they propose.

lecciones.content_es:
Los tres grupos

  • Solo gerundio: enjoy, avoid, finish, keep, mind, practice, suggest, consider, deny, imagine, risk, admit.
  • Solo infinitivo: want, need, decide, hope, plan, promise, refuse, agree, manage, afford, offer, seem.
  • Ambos sin cambio: like, love, hate, prefer, start, begin, continue.

Los que cambian de significado

  • I stopped smoking (dejé de fumar) vs. I stopped to smoke (me detuve para fumar).
  • I remember locking the door (recuerdo haberlo hecho) vs. I remembered to lock it (me acordé de hacerlo).
  • He tried calling (probó llamando) vs. He tried to call (intentó llamar).

Después de preposición

Siempre gerundio: interested in helping, capable of changing, instead of complaining, without saying a word.
lecciones.content_en:
The three groups

  • Gerund only: enjoy, avoid, finish, keep, mind, practice, suggest, consider, deny, imagine, risk, admit.
  • Infinitive only: want, need, decide, hope, plan, promise, refuse, agree, manage, afford, offer, seem.
  • Both with no change: like, love, hate, prefer, start, begin, continue.

Verbs that change meaning

  • I stopped smoking (I quit) vs. I stopped to smoke (I paused in order to smoke).
  • I remember locking the door (I recall doing it) vs. I remembered to lock it (I did not forget).
  • He tried calling (as an experiment) vs. He tried to call (he made the effort).

After a preposition

Always a gerund: interested in helping, capable of changing, instead of complaining, without saying a word.

lecciones.content_es:
Obligación

  • must: obligación interna o de quien habla: We must protect the environment.
  • have to: obligación externa, de una norma: You have to wear a helmet.
  • need to: necesidad práctica: We need to act now.

Prohibición y ausencia de obligación

  • mustn't = prohibido: You mustn't litter.
  • don't have to / don't need to = no es necesario.

En pasado y futuro

must no tiene pasado propio: se usa had to. Para el futuro, will have to.

Voz impersonal

En textos normativos se usa la pasiva: Waste must be separated. · Consent has to be given in writing.
lecciones.content_en:
Obligation

  • must: internal obligation, or the speaker's own: We must protect the environment.
  • have to: external obligation, from a rule: You have to wear a helmet.
  • need to: practical necessity: We need to act now.

Prohibition and absence of obligation

  • mustn't = forbidden: You mustn't litter.
  • don't have to / don't need to = it is not necessary.

In the past and the future

must has no past of its own: use had to. For the future, will have to.

Impersonal voice

In regulatory texts the passive is used: Waste must be separated. · Consent has to be given in writing.

lecciones.content_es:
Consejo

  • should / shouldn't: Governments should invest more in education.
  • ought to: equivalente formal.
  • had better: advertencia con consecuencia implícita.

Posibilidad

  • may / might / could: This policy could reduce inequality.
  • may not / might not: posiblemente no.
  • can: posibilidad general o teórica: Pollution can cause serious illnesses.

Modales perfectos en argumentación

The crisis could have been avoided. · They should have acted earlier. · The data must have been incomplete.

Registro

En un ensayo se prefiere may y could a maybe, y se evita el exceso de must, que suena imperativo.
lecciones.content_en:
Advice

  • should / shouldn't: Governments should invest more in education.
  • ought to: a formal equivalent.
  • had better: a warning with an implied consequence.

Possibility

  • may / might / could: This policy could reduce inequality.
  • may not / might not: possibly not.
  • can: general or theoretical possibility: Pollution can cause serious illnesses.

Perfect modals in argumentation

The crisis could have been avoided. · They should have acted earlier. · The data must have been incomplete.

Register

In an essay may and could are preferred over maybe, and too much must is avoided because it sounds commanding.

lecciones.content_es:
Tres usos según el tiempo

  • Presente irreal: I wish I had more time. (verbo en pasado simple; con to be se prefiere were)
  • Pasado irreal / arrepentimiento: I wish I had studied more. (pasado perfecto)
  • Queja o deseo de cambio: I wish people would recycle. (would + base, para lo que otro hace y molesta)

If only

Es lo mismo pero más enfático: If only we had acted earlier!

Cuidado con would

No se dice I wish I would have. Con el mismo sujeto se usa could: I wish I could help.

Comparación

I hope it rains (posible) vs. I wish it rained (no está lloviendo, deseo irreal).
lecciones.content_en:
Three uses depending on the time

  • Unreal present: I wish I had more time. (past simple; with to be prefer were)
  • Unreal past / regret: I wish I had studied more. (past perfect)
  • Complaint or desired change: I wish people would recycle. (would + base, for what someone else does that annoys you)

If only

The same, but more emphatic: If only we had acted earlier!

Careful with would

Do not say I wish I would have. With the same subject use could: I wish I could help.

Comparison

I hope it rains (possible) vs. I wish it rained (it is not raining; an unreal wish).

lecciones.t: Justicia global y expresión de opiniones
lecciones.content_es:
Justicia y derecho internacional

justice, injustice, impunity, accountability, crimes against humanity, genocide, war crime, international court, trial, verdict, victim, reparation, truth commission.

Estructurar una postura

  • Tesis: I firmly believe that… · This essay argues that…
  • Argumento: To begin with… · Moreover… · What is more…
  • Ejemplo: A clear example of this is… · According to…
  • Contraargumento: Some people claim that… However…
  • Cierre: To sum up… · In conclusion…

Verbos de opinión matizada

claim (afirmar sin probar), argue, point out, suggest, acknowledge (reconocer), deny, emphasize.

Registro

En un texto argumentativo se evita I think repetido: es mejor It can be argued that… o The evidence suggests…
lecciones.content_en:
Justice and international law

justice, injustice, impunity, accountability, crimes against humanity, genocide, war crime, international court, trial, verdict, victim, reparation, truth commission.

Structuring a stance

  • Thesis: I firmly believe that… · This essay argues that…
  • Argument: To begin with… · Moreover… · What is more…
  • Example: A clear example of this is… · According to…
  • Counterargument: Some people claim that… However…
  • Closing: To sum up… · In conclusion…

Nuanced opinion verbs

claim (to assert without proof), argue, point out, suggest, acknowledge, deny, emphasize.

Register

In an argumentative text avoid repeating I think: prefer It can be argued that… or The evidence suggests…

repaso.titulo: Repaso — Expressing Opinions and Social Awareness
repaso.titulo_en: Review — Expressing Opinions and Social Awareness
repaso.resumen_es:
Lo esencial del periodo

Argumentar exige tres herramientas: los patrones verbales (gerundio o infinitivo), los modales para graduar obligación, consejo y posibilidad, y I wish / If only para señalar lo que debería ser distinto.

Puntos gramaticales

  • stop, remember y try cambian de sentido según lleven gerundio o infinitivo.
  • Después de preposición siempre va gerundio.
  • mustn't = prohibido; don't have to = innecesario. El pasado de must es had to.
  • I wish + pasado (presente irreal), + pasado perfecto (arrepentimiento), + would (queja).

Vocabulario

Lugares y útiles escolares, derechos humanos, ambiente, justicia global y fórmulas de registro académico.
repaso.resumen_en:
The core of the term

Arguing requires three tools: verb patterns (gerund or infinitive), modals to grade obligation, advice and possibility, and I wish / If only to signal what should be different.

Grammar points

  • stop, remember and try change meaning depending on gerund or infinitive.
  • After a preposition always use a gerund.
  • mustn't = forbidden; don't have to = unnecessary. The past of must is had to.
  • I wish + past (unreal present), + past perfect (regret), + would (complaint).

Vocabulary

School places and supplies, human rights, the environment, global justice and academic register formulas.
